subject: Next steps and deployment options — BrightPath evaluation
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Liu <ethan.liu@brightpath.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps and deployment options — BrightPath evaluation

Hi Ethan —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap and a few questions so we can scope the right evaluation path (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private):

Recap from our call:
- Core use case: multi-turn summarization + entity enrichment for customer support transcripts.
- Expected concurrent users for Phase 1: ~3-5 per second, with peak bursts.
- Latency expectation: p95 < 500ms for short prompts, up to 2s acceptable for longer requests.

What we need from you to recommend the best deployment mode:
1) Traffic profile: rough peaks (requests/sec) and average requests per minute. If you have a 24h distribution that's ideal.
2) Typical token counts: average request tokens and worst-case tokens (including system + user tokens). You mentioned some long transcripts — ballpark numbers help.
3) Data residency / connectivity needs: do you require VPC peering or on-prem network connectivity for inference?

Hosted quickstart details (what we can stand up fast):
- Quickstart account: sandbox API key + demo endpoints.
- Default rate limits: per-key 60 requests/sec and 10k tokens/sec aggregate for trial (adjustable per-customer).
- Streaming + function-calling supported.
- Security: encrypted at-rest and in-transit; SOC 2 summary available (I can share the report).

If you expect steady high sustained throughput (e.g., >200 req/sec or consistent multi-GPU throughput), Dedicated may be a better economic fit. Private (VPC or on-prem) is recommended when strict network isolation or specific compliance requirements exist.

Proposed next steps:
- Can you confirm the three items above (traffic, token sizes, connectivity) by EOD Thursday?
- I can provision a hosted eval account today and increase rate limits if you need to exercise bursts for load testing.
- Laura (CC'd) will pull SOC2 artifacts and a short network checklist; Aditya will prepare a pricing snapshot for Dedicated/Private options.

Attachments: [Attachment: SOW_v1.pdf] (stub) and I'll send the demo recording once processed.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick follow-up with your infra/proc team if that helps.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks Kimberly — great walkthrough. A few clarifications from our side (cc'ing procurement to loop them in):

Quick answers:
- Peak burst target: we expect up to ~120 requests/sec during business hours for Phase 1 spikes; sustained baseline closer to 25–40 req/sec.
- Token counts: average end-to-end ~700 tokens (some requests are ~300; heavy cases up to ~3k when we include long transcripts plus system prompts).
- Data residency: we prefer US-only data residency. For Phase 2 we may need VPC peering (we'll confirm exact requirements with our security team).

Questions:
1) Can hosted trial rate limits be increased to 200 req/sec for short load tests? Is that per-key or per-account?
2) Do you have per-minute / per-user burst controls? We want to simulate sudden spikes from many users.
3) For Dedicated pricing: can you provide a ballpark monthly range (GPU count / license) so procurement has a sense before a formal RFP?
4) Security: please share SOC2 summary and any network checklist (what inbound/outbound ports, IP ranges, peering options).

Also please share the demo recording when available. I'll schedule a short call with our infra lead (coming Friday morning PT) pending your availability.
